title: Where the region's water goes
scope: Amu Darya and Syr Darya basins, 965,725 km2, 7,445 level-12 basins

method.name: Water Flow Diagram (WFD)
method.description: A methodology for integrated water balancing that connects WASH, IWRM and the human right to water and sanitation, visualising abstraction, distribution, consumption, wastewater and losses for a municipality so stakeholders can see where water goes. Developed with case studies including Bern and St Gallen (Switzerland), Tarapoto (Peru), Agadir (Morocco), Pespire (Honduras) and Santa Maria Bulacan (Philippines).
method.adaptation: This diagram follows the method's intent and departs from its scale. The published applications are municipal, where a utility can account for abstraction, delivery and non-revenue water. Nothing at that resolution is published for this region, so the diagram is drawn at basin-system scale and every flow carries how it is known rather than being rendered alike.

measured.label: Measured
measured.meaning: This project's observation record or plant inventory. Reproducible from the published release.

administered.label: Administered
administered.meaning: Published by the bodies that allocate the water. What was allocated and diverted, not an independent measurement of what flowed.

derived.label: Derived
derived.meaning: Arithmetic on the above, with the operation stated on the flow.

unquantified.label: Not quantified
unquantified.meaning: A flow the method expects and no source here supplies. Drawn as a gap rather than omitted, so its absence is visible.

nodes.label: Not accounted for
nodes.note: The difference between the climatic surplus and recorded diversion. It includes river outflow, wetland and delta losses, aquifer recharge, and the mismatch between two models on different grids. It is not spare water.

nodes.label: Withdrawn above Chardara
nodes.note: Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. The published 2022 total is bounded at the Shardara reservoir and is not split by country; the country figures available are 2026 limits, tabulated separately rather than drawn at a width that would imply they are the same year.

nodes.label: Kazakhstan
nodes.note: Downstream of Chardara. Its withdrawal is outside the 13.83 km3 above, and is published as a limit rather than an actual.

nodes.label: Northern Aral Sea
nodes.note: Fed by the Syr Darya below Chardara

nodes.label: Large Aral Sea
nodes.note: Inflow in 2022 came entirely from drainage canals, not from river discharge

nodes.label: Uzbekistan sectoral use
nodes.note: Sectoral shares are national and are applied here to what remains of the country's Amu Darya diversion after the delta

nodes.label: Returned to rivers and the delta
Distribution losses
nodes.note: Central to the method and often the largest single finding in its published applications. No baseline is published for this region: the 2023 national plan targets a 10 per cent reduction without stating what from.

nodes.label: Groundwater abstraction
nodes.note: The method separates surface from groundwater sources. National usable groundwater is given as 0.5 km3/yr against an estimated 27.6 km3/yr yield, but abstraction is not published at any scale this diagram can use.

nodes.label: Untreated wastewater
nodes.note: The inventory carries 53 plants and the volume they treat. What is generated and never reaches a plant is the quantity the method most wants and no source here reports.

sources.name: Interstate Commission for Water Coordination, Basin Water Organizations
sources.role: BWO Amu Darya and BWO Syr Darya are the inter-ministerial bodies that set and record withdrawal limits and deliveries for the two basins. They are the administering authority, so their figures are what was allocated and diverted, not an independent measurement of what flowed.

sources.role: Basin and country diversion figures for the 2022 hydrological year.

sources.name: CAWater-Info Yearbook 2023, Section 5: Key water developments, Uzbekistan
sources.role: National totals by source and the sectoral shares.

sources.name: SIC ICWC analytical report 2023
sources.role: Context for reservoir inflow and basin conditions; not the source of any figure recorded here.

sources.name: UzGeoData observation record
sources.role: Precipitation, evapotranspiration and runoff, monthly for 7,445 level-12 basins, 2003-2024. Converted to volumes using published basin areas.

sources.name: UzGeoData wastewater plant inventory
sources.role: 53 plants with discharge in cubic metres per day, population served, treatment level and outfall basin.

sources.name: ICWC 91st session, Ashgabat, November 2025 — Syr Darya allocations for 2026
sources.role: Country allocation limits for the Syr Darya by growing and non-growing season. These are limits for 2026, not actuals for 2022, and are drawn as such: the two are not interchangeable and the diagram says which it is showing.

reuse.statement: The reuse terms of the ICWC and SIC ICWC pages have not been established. The figures are reproduced here as published statistics with their source and retrieval date, which is how a citation works and is not the same as a licence. Before this diagram is presented as a product rather than a working case study, those terms need checking with SIC ICWC, and this field replaced with what they say.

reading.scale: Basin systems, not municipalities. Withdrawal here is administered by country and canal system while the record is organised by catchment, and canal delivery crosses basin divides, so a national figure cannot be honestly disaggregated to a basin.
reading.years: The measured fluxes are 22-year means; the administered figures are the 2022 hydrological year. They are drawn together because that is what is published, and the mismatch is stated rather than hidden by averaging one to the other.
reading.closure: This diagram does not close, and is not made to. Precipitation less evapotranspiration leaves a surplus larger than the recorded diversion, while the runoff series exceeds that surplus outright: two models on different grids disagree, and forcing the arrows to balance would hide exactly the thing worth seeing.
reading.colour: Colour is how a flow is known, not what kind of water it is. That is the division this region's data makes necessary and it is the question a reader of a Sankey usually cannot answer.
